title: Sentinel Window Coordinator: Dynamic Linger & Priority Tuning for Continuous Batcher
author: Riya Patel
release_notes: Introduces the Sentinel Window Coordinator which dynamically adjusts linger windows and soft-priority credits to reduce starvation and 99th percentile latency in the continuous batcher. Config knobs added for fine-grained tuning; safe defaults provided. No API breaking changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Continuous batching is critical for cost-efficient LLM inference but has historically been susceptible to starvation and fairness issues when a small number of KV-pinned, long-lived requests monopolize batch slots. We observed multi-tenant tails where a tenant with heavy KV pin churn would push other latency-sensitive requests behind and force repeated preemptions. This PR introduces the 'Sentinel Window Coordinator' — a light-weight runtime component that monitors request age/kv-pin patterns and adjusts per-slot linger windows and a soft-priority credit reservoir to protect latency SLOs while keeping batching efficiency.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a sentinel detector that tags "linger-sentinels": requests whose KV-pin age and sequence length indicate they are likely to linger and prevent window coalescing.
- Introduces a dynamic sentinel_window_ms that shrinks or expands the batcher linger window around these sentinels to avoid prolonged head-of-line blocking.
- Implements a soft-priority credit reservoir (priority_credit_pool) that provides temporary high-priority execution credits to latency-sensitive tenants when sentinel-induced blocking is detected. Credits decay over configurable soft_credit_decay_ms to avoid starvation of batch efficiency.
- Adds a probe/rehab routine that periodically samples long-waiting slots and opportunistically allows small hedged attempts to reclaim progress for starved requests.
- Exposes operational knobs via continuous_batcher.* config (sentinel_window_ms, kv_pin_age_threshold_ms, soft_credit_decay_ms, probe_interval_ms, fairness_target_ratio).

Design notes and rationale:
- Conservative defaults: sentinel_window_ms defaults to 8ms (slightly below the default linger) and kv_pin_age_threshold_ms defaults to 120ms so only genuinely sticky requests are considered sentinels. This reduces churn for normal workloads.
- Soft credits are not global priorities; they are transient tokens granted when the coordinator detects 99th percentile queueing imbalance over a sliding 5s window. Credits are throttled per-tenant to prevent resource monopolization.
- Probe routine uses exponentially bounded retries to avoid thundering-herd effects.
- This design favors graceful degradation: when credits run out, the system reverts to standard continuous batching behavior; all transitions are telemetry-emitted for analysis.

Implementation highlights:
- pkg/batcher/sentinel_coordinator.go: new coordinator, sentinel detector, and probe loop (main logic and state machine).
- pkg/batcher/coordinator_integration.go: hooks to adjust linger windows and consult priority_credit_pool before admitting a request into a batch.
- pkg/scheduler/priority_reservoir.go: new soft-priority pool implementation with decay and per-tenant accounting.
- internal/metrics/batcher_sentinal_metrics.go: new metrics (batcher.sentinel.detected, batcher.sentinel.adjustments, priority_pool.grants, priority_pool.reclaims).
- cmd/bench/bench_continuous_sentinel.sh: microbenchmark script to reproduce tail cases.
- docs/operational/continuous-batcher-sentinels.md: operational guide and tuning tips.
- tests/integration/sentinel_flow_test.go and tests/unit/priority_reservoir_test.go: coverage for coordinator state transitions and credit accounting.

Benchmarks and results:
- Setup: 8xV100-like GPU emulation cluster, synthetic mix: 70% throughput-oriented (long seq) requests, 30% latency-sensitive (short seq). Baseline: main@2026-02-01 with current continuous batcher.
- Key results (latency p99, same QPS):
  - Baseline p99: 158ms
  - With Sentinel Coordinator p99: 86ms (46% improvement)
  - Median and p50 unchanged within noise (±3%)
  - Throughput impact: steady-state token throughput within 2% of baseline (cost neutral)
- Microbench: under synthetic pathological KV-pin churn (kv_pin_age frequently > 200ms), tail improved from 430ms -> 180ms.

Operational considerations:
- Toggle: system can enable/disable coordinator via continuous_batcher.enable_sentinels (default true).
- Observability: added metrics and logs for sentinel detection and credit grants. We recommend enabling batcher.sentinel.* traces for first-rollout in production to validate defaults.
- Backwards compatibility: no external API changes. Config defaults are conservative to minimize regression risk.

Review conversation (excerpt):
- Marisa Duarte (reviewer): "Nice approach. Two main asks: (1) add a unit test that simulates two tenants where one abuses credits to ensure per-tenant limits work, (2) reduce default sentinel_window_ms to 6ms - I'm worried about over-eager window shrinking."
- Riya (author): "Added per-tenant abuse unit test and added metrics to surface per-tenant grant rates. Lowered sentinel_window_ms to 8ms as a compromise and added doc guidance; will follow up with canary telemetry to evaluate default. See commit e6a7cde and tests updated."
- Ethan Kim: "Please ensure the probe routine does not trigger heavy I/O; replace full wake-ups with event-driven hints."
- Riya (author): "Probe now uses admission hint API instead of full scan; updated implementation and tests."

CI and gating: initial CI run had a flaky integration test failure (timeout in sentinel_flow_test). I repro'd locally and tightened the probe loop backoff logic (commit e6a7cde). Rerun CI: all checks green (unit, integration, lint, go vet).

Merge details: Squash-and-merge to main, merge commit includes condensed changelog and links to ENG-3264/ENG-3291. Post-merge actions: schedule a 48h staged canary across two lowest-traffic regions, enable additional telemetry retention for sentinel metrics.

Notes for on-call / SRE: If you see a sudden increase in priority_pool.grants or long sequences of priority_pool.reclaims, consider temporary disablement via continuous_batcher.enable_sentinels=false and engage infra for rollback. The docs page includes a checklist for rollback and safe tuning ranges.

Related work: This PR complements earlier fairness and aging work (see PRs addressing slot reservation and soft timeouts) but takes a runtime-coordinator approach rather than static slot accounting; it proved simpler to reason about per-tenant fairness while preserving batching efficiency.

Future work: per-model heuristics, auto-tuning fairness_target_ratio using observed SLO violations, and extending sentinel detection to consider KV cache hit patterns.

Summary: Adds a pragmatic coordinator that reduced p99 latency substantially in our tests without regressing throughput or cost. Conservative defaults and observability aim to make rollout low-risk.
